verdicts.reason: A: the sneaker is lifted off its disc and sits on top of it like a lid, there is a large dead gap between the headline and subtitle, and the logo floats far above the copy. B: the sneaker is moved to the left, away from the disc, so the disc sits empty bottom-right, and the logo is centred over a right-aligned text column; it strays further from the original.

A keeps the original composition intact (logo, headline, subtitle, sneaker on disc, badge), but it is just the banner placed in a middle band, with big empty areas above and below. B separates the sneaker from its disc, leaving the disc empty and orphaned, and squeezes the text into a right column with a centred logo that doesn't line up with it.

A separates the sneaker from its disc and leaves the disc empty, 'botanicals' runs nearly to the right edge, and the subtitle is jammed against the disc. B lays the headline and subtitle over the beige disc, so 'three' and 'pick your favourite.' turn into white-on-beige and can't be read, which is a clear collision.

A runs the headline ('three') and subtitle ('can pick your favourite.') into the beige disc, so that text is unreadable, and the sneaker is detached from the disc. B keeps the original arrangement with the sneaker on the disc and good hierarchy, but it is the banner scaled into a centre band, with large empty space at the top and bottom of the square.
